#### The Happiness Gap: Where Canada’s Young Adults Thrive

```{r}
library(cansim)

health <- get_cansim("13-10-0905-01")

life_satisfaction <- health %>% filter(
	GEO != "Canada (excluding territories)",
	REF_DATE == "2024",
	Indicators=="Life satisfaction, satisfied or very satisfied",
	`Age group`== "18 to 34 years",
	Sex == "Both sexes",
	Characteristics == "Percent",
	) %>% 
	select(GEO, GeoUID, VALUE)

```

---

```{r echo=FALSE}
life_satisfaction %>% knitr::kable()
```


---

##### Practice: Show the life satisfaction survey results on a map

Generate the map on next slide.

---

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.width=6, fig.height=3, out.width="120%"}
library(cancensus)
pr_sf <- get_census("CA21", list("C"="01"), level="PR", geo_format = "sf") %>% 
	select(GeoUID)

life_satisfaction_pr_sf <- pr_sf %>% left_join(life_satisfaction, by="GeoUID")

ggplot(life_satisfaction_pr_sf) + 
	geom_sf(aes(fill=VALUE)) +
	geom_sf_text(aes(label= paste0(GEO, "\n", VALUE, "%")),color="grey", size=3) +
	scale_fill_continuous(guide=F) +
	coord_sf(ylim = c(42, 63)) +
	labs(title = "Life satisfaction\nsatisfied or very satisfied\n", caption = "Source: Health indicator statistics, StatCan table: 13-10-0905-01") +
	theme_void()
```
